I’ve been farming this land in Quzhou for half a century, and at 72 I know every inch of my 6.5 mu. I farm alone, so I can’t afford backbreaking labor or risky experiments—I need reliability and efficiency. The wheat-maize rotation here on the North China Plain is tight, and with well irrigation I control my water, but I’m careful not to waste it. I’ve kept up with extension recommendations over the years, so I use improved varieties and balanced fertilizer, but I also listen to my own experience with this soil.

For winter wheat, I’ll plant an improved variety on the full 6.5 mu after rotary tillage in early October. I’ll apply about 16 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I’ll irrigate three times: once before winter to ensure safe overwintering, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Two pesticide applications will do—one pre-emergence herbicide and one fungicide/insecticide spray if the weather turns humid. I expect around 580 kg per mu if the spring is kind.

For summer maize, time is everything after the early June wheat harvest. I’ll sow a high-yield hybrid immediately, using no-tillage to save time and labor, though I might do light rotary tillage if the stubble is too thick. I’ll apply roughly 15 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu, since the wheat residue and remaining nutrients help. I’ll irrigate twice: once at sowing if the soil is dry, and again at the big trumpet stage. Two pesticide applications—one herbicide and one insecticide for corn borer—should suffice. I’m counting on about 620 kg per mu.
